title: Standard electrode potentials
competency: Use the standard hydrogen electrode and Table 2.3 to find E°cell and predict whether redox reactions are spontaneous.

keywords.def: Pt in 1 M H⁺ with H₂ at 1 atm; its E° is defined as 0.00 V.
E° of a half-reaction written as a reduction, at 1 M, 1 atm and 25 °C.
A species on the left of a half-reaction reacts with a species on the right of any half-reaction below it in Table 2.3.

en.text: A single electrode potential cannot be measured, so the standard hydrogen electrode (Pt, H₂ at 1 atm, 1 M H⁺) is defined as 0.00 V. Any half-cell joined to it gives its standard reduction potential E°. Always written as reductions, these combine as E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode: Zn −0.76 V and Cu +0.34 V give the Daniell cell 1.10 V.

am.text: መደበኛ የሃይድሮጅን ኤሌክትሮድ 0.00 V ተብሎ ይወሰዳል። E°cell = E°ካቶድ − E°አኖድ። ዳኒዬል ሴል 1.10 V ይሰጣል።

screens.title: One electrode alone?
screens.ask: Can you measure the voltage of a single zinc electrode on its own?
opts: No, only the difference between two electrodes
screens.after: A voltmeter needs two electrodes. So we pick a reference, the hydrogen electrode, and call it 0.00 V.

screens.title: The standard hydrogen electrode
paras: Pt electrode, H₂ at 1 atm, in 1 M H⁺, at 25 °C.
Zn with SHE: 0.76 V, Zn is the anode, so E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V.
Cu with SHE: 0.34 V, Cu is the cathode, so E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.

screens.title: Some standard reduction potentials (25 °C)
paras: Strongest oxidizing agent at the top; strongest reducing agent at the bottom.

screens.ask: Br₂ + Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2Br⁻ has E°cell = 1.83 V; E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V. E°(Br₂/Br⁻) = ___ V
screens.clue: Bromine is reduced: it is the cathode.

en.text: The higher E°, the stronger the oxidizing agent (F₂ is strongest); the lower E°, the stronger the reducing agent (Li is strongest). A reaction is spontaneous under standard conditions if E°cell > 0: a species on the left of a half-reaction reacts with a species on the right of any half-reaction below it (the diagonal rule). E° does not change when a half-reaction is multiplied, but changes sign when reversed.

am.text: E° ከፍ ሲል ጠንካራ ኦክሳይድ አድራጊ ነው። E°cell > 0 ሲሆን ግብረመልሱ ድንገተኛ ነው (የሰያፍ ደንብ)። E° በማባዛት አይለወጥም።

screens.title: Try a pair
screens.ask: Pick E° of the cathode and of the anode. When is the cell reaction spontaneous?
screens.note: Positive: spontaneous. Negative: the reverse reaction is spontaneous.

screens.title: Using the table
paras: Higher E°: greater tendency to be reduced; stronger oxidizing agent.
Lower E°: stronger reducing agent (Li strongest).
Diagonal rule: left of an upper half-reaction + right of a lower one react.
E° is intensive: 2Ag⁺ + 2e⁻ → 2Ag still has +0.80 V.
Reversing a half-reaction changes the sign of E°.

defs: A species on the left of a half-reaction reacts with a species on the right of any half-reaction below it in Table 2.3.

screens.text: The strongest oxidizing agent in Table 2.3 is
screens.why: It has the most positive E° (+2.87 V).
screens.clue: Look at the top of the table.

screens.text: Can Sn (E° −0.14 V) reduce Zn²⁺ (E° −0.76 V)?
screens.why: Zn²⁺ would be the cathode: −0.76 − (−0.14) = −0.62 V, so not spontaneous.
screens.clue: Which is the stronger reducing agent, Sn or Zn?

screens.why: E° is intensive: multiplying the equation does not change it.
screens.clue: Does a bigger electrode change the voltage?

screens.text: Which species react with Al³⁺ (E° −1.66 V)?
screens.why: Only metals with E° below −1.66 V can reduce Al³⁺: Mg (−2.37), K (−2.93).
screens.clue: They must be stronger reducing agents than Al.

screens.text: Which metal reduces Fe²⁺ (−0.44 V) but NOT Zn²⁺ (−0.76 V)?
screens.clue: Its E° must lie between −0.76 V and −0.44 V.

notes.text: Table 2.3 misprints (E° values are fine): PbO₂ + 4H⁺ (not 4H⁻) → PbSO₄; Ce⁴⁺ + e⁻ → Ce³⁺; Cl₂ (not 2Cl); Cr₂O₇²⁻; NO₃⁻(aq) → NO(g); MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻; SO₄²⁻ → SO₂ (not NO₂).

p.104: Li⁺ takes one electron (book prints 2e⁻); strictly F⁻, not F₂, is the weakest reducing agent. p.100: H₂ is at 1 atm, not "1M". p.102: the Daniell cell is Figure 2.9, and the line should begin "E°cell =".
